candidates.detail: compile_building_collision builds a map from resolved solid IDs, selects host IDs for walls not replaced by another owner, then uses filter_map to look each selected ID up. A selected ID absent from the map never reaches collision_parts and does not itself produce a CollisionError. If the remaining selected parts, window bars and bounds compile successfully, the function can return a BuildingCollision assembled without that wall-host part. A separately compiled bar has its own opening-derived source; no assertion is made that every possible missing ID has no other coincident geometry.
candidates.conditional_case: Take a BuildingPlan with an unreplaced wall referencing host ID X and remove X from resolved_geometry.solids while leaving the wall reference. The public plan, wall and resolved-geometry fields permit this in-memory state; no particular generator output is claimed. Selection still includes X, its map lookup yields none, and the source filter skips it. The source auditor reports invalid_wall_host_union for a missing referenced host if audit execution reaches that check. The collision compiler does not call that auditor. This is source reasoning only; no plan was constructed, no compile, audit, physics or gameplay was run.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: The ordinary tactical server scene-building path calls generate(program), then compile_building_collision and maps returned cuboids into an Avian compound static collider. The regular generate function explicitly delegates to generate_unchecked and documents exhaustive audit as an explicit operation; this does not prove its builders produce inconsistent references. The separate generate_document path calls validate_generated_plan, which invokes audit_plan and rejects issues. Existing accepted/consistent plans retain all selected wall hosts, and operable closures are intentionally separate. No supported production plan with a missing host, returned collider, traversal effect or use of a mutated public plan is established.
